# Build & Toolchain

minix.rs builds as a single Cargo workspace. There is no separate C build today
(the musl fork is future work — see [Roadmap](roadmap.md)); the only non-Cargo
step is fetching the prebuilt Limine binary, and a couple of shell scripts in
`tools/` stage the boot ESP and launch QEMU.

## Prerequisites

- **Rust nightly**, pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` (a bare `nightly` would let new
  lints or fmt rules break the build with no code change).
- **QEMU** with `qemu-system-aarch64`.
- **aarch64 UEFI firmware** (edk2 / OVMF). `tools/qemu-run.sh` auto-detects it in
  common locations, or set `QEMU_EFI_AARCH64=/path/to/edk2-aarch64-code.fd`.

## Quick start

```sh
# One-time: fetch the pinned Limine binary into external/limine/dist/
make -C external/limine

# Build the kernel for aarch64 (the primary target)
cargo kernel-aarch64

# Build + boot under QEMU. The kernel runs indefinitely once EL0 starts, so a
# timeout is mandatory. Redirect to a file when you need to grep the log.
timeout 8 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release

# Clean, stub-free boot for debugging: --no-default-features disables the
# `boot-stubs` feature, so only the servers + init/worker boot (no demo stubs
# A-D flooding the trace). See "Boot stubs" under Cargo workspace below.
timeout 8 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release --no-default-features
```

`cargo run` invokes the cargo runner (`tools/qemu-run.sh`), which stages an ESP
directory at `target/esp/`, drops Limine and the freshly built kernel in, and
boots QEMU with the directory-as-FAT helper — no disk-image scripting needed (see
[Boot](boot/overview.md) for the ESP layout and the exact QEMU command). Early
serial output looks like:

```text
minix.rs booting on aarch64
HHDM offset: 0xffff000000000000
```

## Cargo workspace

The root `Cargo.toml` declares every crate as a workspace member: `kernel`,
`kernel-shared`, `minix-ipc`, `server-rt`, the six `servers/*`, the (stub)
`drivers/*` and `fs/*`, and `userland/{init,worker,sh,coreutils}`.

The kernel builds against the **builtin `aarch64-unknown-none` target** — not a
custom JSON spec. `.cargo/config.toml` wires the details:

```toml
[target.aarch64-unknown-none]
runner   = "tools/qemu-run.sh"
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-Tkernel/src/arch/aarch64/linker.ld"]

[alias]
kernel-aarch64 = "build -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release"
```

The `x86_64-unknown-none` target and its `kernel-x86_64` alias are scaffolding for
the planned port; the kernel does not boot on x86_64 yet.

### Assembly and the boot image (`kernel/build.rs`)

The kernel's `build.rs` does two build-time jobs:

- **Assembly** — it assembles the kernel's `.S` files with `clang` and passes the
  resulting objects straight to the linker. When `CARGO_CFG_TARGET_OS != "none"` it
  instead emits a `cargo::error=` line and stops, because a host build of the kernel
  is always a mistake (see [The kernel is not host-buildable](#the-kernel-is-not-host-buildable)).
  The demo-stub blob `user_stub.S` is assembled only when the `boot-stubs` feature is
  on (see [Boot stubs](#boot-stubs-boot-stubs-feature)).
- **Boot-image packing** — it builds each boot server for the EL0 user target in
  its own isolated `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, packs the ELFs into the MXBI archive
  (`pack_mxbi`), and emits `BOOT_IMAGE_PATH` for the kernel to `include_bytes!`.
  There is no separate `mkbootimage` tool. See [Boot](boot/overview.md) for the
  archive format and module set.

### Boot stubs (`boot-stubs` feature)

The kernel installs four hand-written EL0 demo stubs A–D at boot — a live
regression battery for the IPC primitives (A↔B ping-pong), SCHED delegation (C),
and the VM page-fault / SIGSEGV path (D). They are useful but noisy: stub C's
`SYS_GETINFO` loop floods the trace. The **`boot-stubs` cargo feature (default-on)**
gates them, so `--no-default-features` yields a clean boot of servers + init/worker
only.

The feature lives on two crates — the **kernel** (gates the stub code in
`arch::aarch64::userland`) and **PM** (gates the stub `mproc` seeding). Because
`build.rs` builds each server in a *separate* nested cargo invocation with its own
feature resolution, it reads `CARGO_FEATURE_BOOT_STUBS` and, when the kernel is
stub-free, passes `--no-default-features` to the nested PM build too — keeping the
two in lockstep. The feature is intentionally **not** placed on `kernel-shared`: a
shared-crate default feature is force-enabled by other dependents (`minix-ipc`,
`server-rt`) through cargo *feature unification* and could not be turned off. So
`NR_STUB_PROCS` (= 4) and `FORK_POOL_BASE` (= 15) are constant regardless of the
feature — disabling stubs merely leaves proc slots 11–14 unoccupied; it does not
renumber the fork pool.

## Host tests

Logic that can run off-target lives in `kernel-shared` and in the host-testable
server crates:

```sh
cargo test -p minixrs-kernel-shared
```

`cargo test -p minixrs-kernel` runs **zero** tests by design — every kernel module
is gated on `#[cfg(target_os = "none")]`. QEMU is the primary verification for
kernel code; CI smoke-boots it (below).

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on every PR and on pushes to `main`. Nine jobs run
in parallel:

| Job | Blocking? | What it checks |
|-----|-----------|----------------|
| `fmt` | yes | `cargo fmt --all --check` |
| `clippy` | yes | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (host target) |
| `audit` | yes | `cargo-audit` advisory scan |
| `deny` | yes | `cargo-deny` (licenses / bans, config in `deny.toml`) |
| `geiger` | advisory | `unsafe` surface report |
| `miri` | advisory | UB check on the host-testable crates |
| `qemu-smoke` | advisory | boots the kernel and greps the serial log |
| `coverage` | yes | `cargo-llvm-cov` → `lcov.info` |
| `sonar` | — | feeds LCOV to SonarQube Cloud |

Notes: the blocking `clippy --workspace` gate runs on the **host** target, where
the kernel's real modules are `cfg`-gated out — so kernel code is not clippy-linted
by CI; `cargo kernel-aarch64` is the real compile gate for it. `qemu-smoke`

advisory until it proves stable. `Cargo.lock` is committed so `audit` / `deny` are
reproducible, and third-party actions are pinned to commit SHAs.

`--all-targets`: the kernel is `no_std`/`no_main`, so there is no test harness to build.
`qemu-smoke` (also `ubuntu-24.04-arm`) boots for 45 s wall clock, requires exit status
124 — the `timeout(1)` status a healthy, never-exiting kernel must produce — and then
runs `tools/check-boot-log.sh` against `tests/qemu-boot.expected` / `.forbidden`; keep
those expectations timing-robust (first occurrences, never counts), because CI's TCG is

## Chunk 7: De-host the kernel crate ◀ ready (branch feature/dehost-kernel, pending merge)

**Goal:** every kernel module was `#[cfg(target_os = "none")]`-gated so host builds
saw an empty crate — which is why kernel code was invisible to the blocking lint
gates. Remove the kernel crate from host builds entirely so the per-item gates can
go away.

**Scope** (bullets 2 and 3 of the original investigation were absorbed by chunk 5,
which shipped the `clippy-kernel` job and cleared the named lints; only bullet 1
remained, plus the follow-through that job's own comment nominated):

- Exclude `minixrs-kernel` from host workspace builds via workspace
  `default-members`; it stays a `members` entry so one `Cargo.lock` keeps
  `audit`/`deny` and `cargo fmt --all` covering it. **`--workspace` overrides
  `default-members`**, so CI's `clippy` and `coverage` jobs pass
  `--exclude minixrs-kernel`, and `geiger`'s per-package sweep filters it out.
- Drop all 15 `cfg(target_os = "none")` gates from `kernel/src/main.rs`
  (unconditional `no_std`/`no_main`, no host `fn main() {}` fallback). Two guards
  make an accidental host build one clear message: `build.rs` emits `cargo::error=`
  before rustc runs, and `main.rs` carries a `compile_error!` mirroring
  `arch/mod.rs`'s arch guard.
- Flip `clippy-kernel` to **blocking** — with the kernel out of every host gate it
  is the only CI job that compiles kernel code at all — and give it a second
  `--no-default-features` run so chunk 3's stub-free config is guarded too.
- Flip `qemu-smoke` to **blocking** (green across PRs #33–#37, satisfying chunk 1's
  "stable across a few PRs" bar) and require its boot step to exit 124.
- Drive-by: `user_va_ok` + `USER_VA_TOP` and their 5 tests move from
  `kernel/src/ipc/message.rs` to `kernel-shared/src/message.rs`. The tests had
  never executed (the module was cfg-gated out on host); de-hosting would have made
  that permanent. `kernel-shared` gains 49 → 54 running tests, and
  `arch/aarch64/addrspace.rs`'s duplicate `USER_VA_TOP` literal is folded in.

**Proof:** host gates green with the kernel excluded; `cargo check --workspace`
fails with exactly one actionable error; `cargo kernel-aarch64` and both QEMU boots
(default + stub-free) unchanged; kernel-target clippy blocking in CI.

The exec target is a freestanding `userland/worker` ELF (getpid loop + `PM_EXIT`; **no** `server-rt`/SEF — a plain user program, deps `minix-ipc` + `kernel-shared` only), packed into the MXBI archive by `build.rs` with sentinel proc_nr `com::EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR = -1` — the boot loader (`userland.rs` load loop) skips any negative proc_nr, so `worker` is resolvable by name but **never boot-loaded** (no `[as]` line, no proc/priv slot). PM's `execve` hardcodes `EXEC_TARGET = "worker"` for the demo (a user-supplied path arrives with Phase-5 musl/filesystem; the kernel path is already name-driven). Stub E's child branch flips `PM_EXIT` → `PM_EXEC`: fork → child execs `worker` → worker exits → parent reaps → loop, so a `[ksys SYS_EXEC] target=16 name=worker` per cycle sits between the `SYS_FORK`/`SYS_EXIT nr=16` twins with a monotonically advancing endpoint generation + recycled ASID (exec teardown + reap proof). `userland/**/src/main.rs` added to `sonar.coverage.exclusions` (freestanding entry point, QEMU-verified, no host-testable logic — like the server `main.rs`es)

- The demo stubs A–D are gated behind a **`boot-stubs` cargo feature (default-on)** — `--no-default-features` gives a clean, stub-free boot (servers + init/worker only) for debugging (chunk-3 prep). The feature lives on **two crates**, the kernel (gates `arch::aarch64::userland`'s stub code) and PM (gates `mproc::seed`'s stub loop), because those are the only two that install/seed stubs. `kernel/build.rs` reads `CARGO_FEATURE_BOOT_STUBS` to (a) drop `user_stub.S` from the assembly `sources` and (b) pass `--no-default-features` to the *nested* PM build (the nested build has its own feature resolution, so the flag must be threaded through), keeping kernel and PM in lockstep. The feature is deliberately **not** on `kernel-shared`: a shared-crate default feature gets force-enabled by other dependents (`minix-ipc`, `server-rt`) via cargo **feature unification**, making it impossible to turn off — so `NR_STUB_PROCS` stays a constant `4` and `FORK_POOL_BASE` (= 15) is stable; disabling stubs just leaves slots 11–14 unoccupied, it doesn't renumber the fork pool

- User-process capacity is one shared constant (chunk-4 prep): `kernel-shared::com::NR_SERVED_PROCS` (= 32) is the exclusive proc-nr ceiling the user-space servers track, and all three per-process server tables derive their size from it — PM `mproc` (`NR_MPROCS = NR_SERVED_PROCS`, proc-nr-indexed), VM `ClientRegions` (`MAX_CLIENTS = NR_SERVED_PROCS`, proc-nr-indexed), and SCHED `policy` (`CAP = NR_SERVED_PROCS`, an *associative* count, not proc-nr-indexed, so `NR_SERVED_PROCS` over-covers the delegatable set). Review this session for learnings about working with Claude Code in this codebase. Update CLAUDE.md with context that would help future Claude sessions be more effective.

## Step 1: Reflect

What context was missing that would have helped Claude work more effectively?
- Bash commands that were used or discovered
- Code style patterns followed
- Testing approaches that worked
- Environment/configuration quirks
- Warnings or gotchas encountered

## Step 2: Find CLAUDE.md Files

```bash
find . -name "CLAUDE.md" -o -name ".claude.local.md" 2>/dev/null | head -20
```

Decide where each addition belongs:
- `CLAUDE.md` - Team-shared (checked into git)
- `.claude.local.md` - Personal/local only (gitignored)

## Step 3: Draft Additions

**Keep it concise** - one line per concept. CLAUDE.md is part of the prompt, so brevity matters.

Format: `<command or pattern>` - `<brief description>`

Avoid:
- Verbose explanations
- Obvious information
- One-off fixes unlikely to recur

## Step 4: Show Proposed Changes

For each addition:

```
### Update: ./CLAUDE.md

**Why:** [one-line reason]

\`\`\`diff
+ [the addition - keep it brief]
\`\`\`
```

## Step 5: Apply with Approval

Ask if the user wants to apply the changes. Only edit files they approve.
Let me verify one candidate learning before proposing it.

content.text:
Reflecting on the session, three candidate learnings — I verified the most important one above.

### Update: `./CLAUDE.md`

**Why:** The documented `timeout 8` boot command is actively misleading — I ran it and got **zero kernel output**. ~3 s goes to the cargo rebuild and the rest to UEFI firmware startup; the kernel never reaches its banner. `check-boot-log.sh` failed all 24 markers.

```diff
-# QEMU under TCG advances *guest* time slower than wall-clock, so a `timeout N`
-# run reaches far fewer than N x 100 ticks. ... and run 20-25 s to observe several periods.
-timeout 8 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release
+# Budget ~5 s of every run for the cargo rebuild + UEFI firmware startup before
+# the kernel's first byte: `timeout 8` yields a log with NO kernel output at all
+# (check-boot-log.sh fails all 24 markers). Use 25 s for anything you intend to
+# verify; QEMU under TCG also advances *guest* time slower than wall-clock, so a
+# `timeout N` run reaches far fewer than N x 100 ticks. ...
+timeout 25 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release
```
(Same for the `--no-default-features` line, and the `timeout 8` inside the "QEMU is the primary verification" conventions bullet.)

### Update: `./CLAUDE.md` — shell gotcha

**Why:** Hit this copying the `qemu-smoke` boot snippet into a local zsh shell; `status=0` aborts with `read-only variable`.

```diff
+ - `status` is read-only in zsh — when adapting the qemu-smoke CI snippet locally, rename the exit-code variable (e.g. `rc=$?`)
```

### Update: `./CLAUDE.md` — fmt coverage diagnostic (lowest value)

**Why:** Used it to prove `cargo fmt --all` still reaches the kernel after de-hosting.

```diff
+ - `cargo fmt --all -v --check` lists the crate roots rustfmt was handed — the way to confirm a crate is still fmt-covered after workspace-membership changes
```

Note: everything else I learned (the `--workspace` / `default-members` override, the `cargo::error=` guard, the no-cfg-gates rule, the rust-analyzer setting, the new blocking gates) is already written into CLAUDE.md as part of the chunk itself.

lines: - The demo stubs A–D are gated behind a **`boot-stubs` cargo feature (default-on)** — `--no-default-features` gives a clean, stub-free boot (servers + init/worker only) for debugging (chunk-3 prep). The feature lives on **two crates**, the kernel (gates `arch::aarch64::userland`'s stub code) and PM (gates `mproc::seed`'s stub loop), because those are the only two that install/seed stubs. `kernel/build.rs` reads `CARGO_FEATURE_BOOT_STUBS` to (a) drop `user_stub.S` from the assembly `sources` and (b) pass `--no-default-features` to the *nested* PM build (the nested build has its own feature resolution, so the flag must be threaded through), keeping kernel and PM in lockstep. The feature is deliberately **not** on `kernel-shared`: a shared-crate default feature gets force-enabled by other dependents (`minix-ipc`, `server-rt`) via cargo **feature unification**, making it impossible to turn off — so `NR_STUB_PROCS` stays a constant `4` and `FORK_POOL_BASE` (= 15) is stable; disabling stubs just leaves slots 11–14 unoccupied, it doesn't renumber the fork pool

- User-process capacity is one shared constant (chunk-4 prep): `kernel-shared::com::NR_SERVED_PROCS` (= 32) is the exclusive proc-nr ceiling the user-space servers track, and all three per-process server tables derive their size from it — PM `mproc` (`NR_MPROCS = NR_SERVED_PROCS`, proc-nr-indexed), VM `ClientRegions` (`MAX_CLIENTS = NR_SERVED_PROCS`, proc-nr-indexed), and SCHED `policy` (`CAP = NR_SERVED_PROCS`, an *associative* count, not proc-nr-indexed, so `NR_SERVED_PROCS` over-covers the delegatable set). Never reintroduce independent capacity literals: each crate carries a `const _: () = assert!(… >= NR_SERVED_PROCS)` guard (plus `NR_SERVED_PROCS <= NR_PROCS` and `> NR_BOOT_PROCS + NR_STUB_PROCS` in com.rs) so an under-sized local edit fails at compile time. VM `MAX_REGIONS` (regions per client, heap + mmaps) is a separate knob (= 16), unrelated to the kernel frame allocator's like-named `MAX_REGIONS` in `mm/frame.rs`

- Feature-toggle debugging: when a `--no-default-features` build doesn't actually drop a feature, suspect cargo **feature unification** — diagnose with `cargo tree -p <crate> --no-default-features -e features -i <shared-crate>` (inverted tree shows *who* still activates it) or `cargo tree -p <crate> -f "{p} {f}"` (feature set per crate)

- `no_std` library crates that host-test via `#![cfg_attr(not(test), no_std)]` get linted in their std test-config too (`clippy --all-targets`): a const-only `assert!(A > B)` trips `assertions_on_constants` (use a module-level `const _: () = assert!(…)` like `callnr.rs`), and a bare `loop {}` in a function present under `test` trips `empty_loop` (use `loop { core::hint::spin_loop() }`; the `#[cfg(not(test))]` panic handler's `loop {}` is exempt because it's absent under test)

- The blocking `clippy --workspace` gate runs `-D warnings`: a doc-comment line starting with `+ ` (or `- `/`* `) parses as a markdown bullet and trips `doc_lazy_continuation` on the following lines — reword so continuation lines don't begin with a list marker

- User-space servers build as freestanding `#![no_std]`/`#![no_main]` ELFs linked with their own `user.ld` (page-aligned PT_LOADs, base `0x10_0000`; kernel sets `sp_el0` so `_start` needs no stack setup). The kernel's `build.rs` builds them for `aarch64-unknown-none` in a *separate* `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` (dodges the nested-cargo build-lock deadlock), overrides the kernel linker script via `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` → the server's `user.ld`, and emits `VM_ELF_PATH` so `kernel/src/boot_image/mod.rs` can `include_bytes!` it. `boot_image/elf.rs` is the minimal ET_EXEC/AArch64 loader (PT_LOAD → `alloc_frame` + HHDM copy + map; BSS via zeroed frames). The multi-module MXBI archive is deferred until Phase 4 loads more than one server

input.body:
Pre-Phase-5 cleanup, chunk 7 (`docs/plans/phase-5-prep.md`).

## Problem

Every kernel module was `#[cfg(target_os = "none")]`-gated so host `--workspace` builds saw an empty crate. That bought a green `cargo check` and nothing else: all 48 kernel source files were invisible to every lint gate, and `kernel/src/ipc/message.rs` carried 5 `#[test]` fns that had **never once executed**.

## What changed

**The kernel leaves host builds entirely.**

- `Cargo.toml` gains `default-members` — all 21 members except `kernel`. It stays a `members` entry deliberately: one shared `Cargo.lock` keeps `audit`/`deny` covering its deps, and `cargo fmt --all` still formats it (cargo-fmt enumerates all *members*, and rustfmt follows `mod` declarations without evaluating `cfg`).
- **`--workspace` overrides `default-members`**, so it is not sufficient on its own — CI's `clippy` and `coverage` jobs now pass `--exclude minixrs-kernel`, and `geiger`'s per-package sweep filters it out.
- All 15 `cfg(target_os = "none")` gates are gone from `main.rs` (unconditional `no_std`/`no_main`, no host `fn main() {}` fallback). Two guards turn an accidental host build into one clear message instead of a cascade: `build.rs` emits `cargo::error=` before rustc runs, and `main.rs` carries a `compile_error!` mirroring `arch/mod.rs`'s arch guard.

**Two gates flip to blocking.** With the kernel out of every host gate, `clippy-kernel` became the only CI job that compiles kernel code at all — so it now blocks, and gains a second `--no-default-features` run covering chunk 3's stub-free config (nothing checked that build before; two `#[allow]`s live only inside `cfg(feature = "boot-stubs")` code). `qemu-smoke` also flips to blocking — it stayed green across PRs #33–#37, satisfying chunk 1's own "stable across a few PRs" bar — and now requires exit 124, the `timeout(1)` status a healthy never-exiting kernel must produce.

**Drive-by:** `user_va_ok` + `USER_VA_TOP` and their 5 tests move to `kernel-shared/src/message.rs`, where they actually run (49 → 54 tests, now also under miri and LCOV). De-hosting would otherwise have made their deadness permanent. `addrspace.rs`'s duplicate `USER_VA_TOP` literal folds into the shared one.

Chunk 7's original bullets 2 and 3 (add a kernel clippy job; triage its lints) were already delivered by chunk 5 in #37 — that chunk's stale `pending merge` marker is reconciled here too. **Chunk 6, the Phase 5 design session, is now the only pre-Phase-5 chunk left.**

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo check --workspace` (negative test) | fails with **exactly one** actionable error naming `cargo kernel-aarch64` |
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | green; still enumerates `kernel/build.rs` + `kernel/src/main.rs` |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude minixrs-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` | green |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (bare, via `default-members`) | green |
| `cargo test -p minixrs-kernel-shared` | 54 passed (was 49; the 5 `user_va_ok` tests now run) |
| `cargo clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none -- -D warnings` | green, both default and `--no-default-features` |
| `cargo kernel-aarch64` | builds |
| QEMU boot, default features, 25 s | exit 124; `check-boot-log.sh` PASS, all 24 markers |
| QEMU boot, `--no-default-features`, 25 s | exit 124; 7 servers + init, no stubs, fork/exec/wait cycling, no forbidden markers |
| `mdbook build book` | green |

Not verified locally: `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --exclude minixrs-kernel` (cargo-llvm-cov isn't installed on this machine). `--exclude` is a documented cargo-llvm-cov flag and the failure mode would be immediate and loud; the `coverage` job on this PR is the confirmation. If it does reject the flag, the fix is to drop `--workspace` and let `default-members` do the selecting.

Also documented, after hitting it this session: `timeout 8` — the value CLAUDE.md and the book previously used in their boot examples — produces a log with **no kernel output at all** (~5 s goes to the cargo rebuild plus UEFI firmware startup). Both now say 25 s.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Chunk 7 is done and open as **[PR #38](https://github.com/minixrs/minixrs/pull/38)**.

## What shipped

**The kernel is out of host builds.** `Cargo.toml` gained `default-members` (all 21 members except `kernel`), and all 15 `cfg(target_os = "none")` gates are gone from `main.rs` — unconditional `no_std`/`no_main`, no host `fn main() {}`.

The key mechanic your plan text didn't anticipate: **`--workspace` overrides `default-members`**, so `default-members` alone doesn't fix CI. The `clippy` and `coverage` jobs pass `--exclude minixrs-kernel`, and `geiger`'s sweep filters it out.

**Two guards** turn an accidental host build into one message instead of a cascade — `build.rs` emits `cargo::error=` before rustc runs, `main.rs` carries a `compile_error!`. Verified: `cargo check --workspace` fails with exactly one actionable error.

**Both gates flipped to blocking.** `clippy-kernel` is now the only CI job that compiles kernel code at all, so it blocks and runs twice (default + `--no-default-features`). `qemu-smoke` blocks and requires exit 124.

**Test relocation:** `user_va_ok` + `USER_VA_TOP` moved to `kernel-shared` — 49 → 54 tests, and the 5 that had never executed now run under miri and LCOV too.

## Scope notes

Chunk 5 had already merged as PR #37, delivering chunk 7's bullets 2 and 3 — only bullet 1 remained. Both plan docs still showed chunk 5 as `pending merge`; reconciled. **Chunk 6 (the Phase 5 design session) is now the only pre-Phase-5 chunk left.**

Two things worth flagging:

- **One command unverified locally.** `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --exclude minixrs-kernel` — cargo-llvm-cov isn't installed here. `--exclude` is documented and the failure would be immediate, but the `coverage` job on this PR is the real confirmation. Fallback if it rejects the flag: drop `--workspace`.
- **`timeout 8` was wrong in the docs.** Running CLAUDE.md's own documented boot command gave *zero* kernel output — ~5 s goes to the rebuild plus UEFI startup, and `check-boot-log.sh` failed all 24 markers. Both CLAUDE.md and the book now say 25 s. I skipped the other two CLAUDE.md additions you declined.

Separately: bare `cargo build` fails on the server/userland crates (`#![no_main]` ELFs can't link against host libc). I confirmed via `git stash` that this is pre-existing on `main`, not a regression — `check`/`clippy`/`test` are the host gates, and CLAUDE.md now says so.

content.text:
Investigated and tested. Here's what I found.

## blog_os doesn't transfer directly

It's a **single crate** that *is* the kernel, so `[build] target = "x86_64-blog_os.json"` in `.cargo/config.toml` is trivially correct — there's nothing host-side. Our workspace is mixed: the bare-metal kernel *plus* genuinely host-tested libraries (kernel-shared's 54 tests, miri, coverage → Sonar). A global `[build] target` would break all of that.

## But the right analogue exists, and it works

Cargo's **`per-package-target`** — `forced-target = "aarch64-unknown-none"` on the kernel package only. Same idea as blog_os (the crate declares its own target), scoped to one member. Tested on your pinned nightly:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| **Your exact RustRover command** | ✅ passes |
| `cargo check --workspace` | ✅ kernel cross-compiled, no error |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` | ✅ **genuinely lints kernel code** — canary caught `needless_bool` + `manual_is_multiple_of` |
| `cargo test --workspace` | ✅ |
| `cargo kernel-aarch64` / QEMU boot | ✅ 24/24 markers |
| `cargo check -p minixrs-kernel --target x86_64-apple-darwin` | ✅ forced-target **wins** — host build is now impossible |

One extra key was needed: `[[bin]] test = false, bench = false` (stable). Without it `--all-targets` builds a phantom test harness that needs `std` — that was the `can't find crate for test` error I hit first.

**This is strictly better than what I merged into the PR.** The de-hosting *hid* kernel code from the lint gates; `forced-target` makes it *visible* to them — the blind spot chunk 7 attacked closes completely rather than moving. And no per-developer IDE config.

## The one real cost

`per-package-target` is an **unstable Cargo feature** (tracking issue [cargo#9406](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9406)), so it needs the `cargo-features = ["per-package-target"]` opt-in and nightly. You already pin a dated nightly precisely to control this kind of churn, and if a bump ever drops it, cargo errors on the manifest loudly — the fallback is exactly the `default-members` approach already in the PR. But it is a new dependency on an unstable feature, which cuts against the repo's stated toolchain-stability philosophy.

My working tree currently has `forced-target` + `[[bin]] test = false` applied on top of the PR branch (uncommitted); `default-members` and the CI `--exclude` flags are still there from the merged commit.

questions.question: Adopt the `forced-target` approach on top of PR #38?

options.label: Yes — adopt it (Recommended)
options.description: Add cargo-features = ["per-package-target"] + forced-target + [[bin]] test=false to kernel/Cargo.toml. RustRover works with zero config, kernel becomes lintable by workspace clippy, host builds become impossible. Accepts a dependency on an unstable Cargo feature, guarded by your dated nightly pin.

options.label: No — keep merged approach
options.description: Leave PR #38 as-is (default-members + --exclude) and fix RustRover per-developer: add `--exclude minixrs-kernel` under Settings → Rust → External Linters → Additional arguments. No unstable features, but kernel code stays invisible to local/workspace clippy and each developer must configure their IDE.

questions.question: If adopted: what happens to the `default-members` exclusion added in PR #38?

options.label: Drop it (Recommended)
options.description: forced-target removes the correctness reason to hide the kernel. Keeping it would make bare `cargo clippy`/`check` silently skip kernel code again — reintroducing the exact blind spot chunk 7 set out to remove. Simpler story: the kernel always builds for aarch64-unknown-none, everywhere.

content.text:
Reverted — working tree is clean and PR #38 is unchanged. Gates still green.

## Fixing RustRover

Your linter command is RustRover's **External Linters** feature. Add the exclusion there:

**Settings → Languages & Frameworks → Rust → External Linters**
- **Additional arguments:** `--exclude minixrs-kernel`

That appends to the existing command, giving `… --all-targets --workspace --features … --exclude minixrs-kernel`, which is valid (`--exclude` requires `--workspace`, which is already present).

If the error also appears from the build action rather than only the on-the-fly linter, the same argument goes in **Settings → Build, Execution, Deployment → Cargo → Additional arguments** (or on the specific run configuration).

Note this lives in `.idea/`, which is gitignored — so it's per-developer, and any new contributor hits the same wall once. That's the tradeoff you accepted in choosing to avoid the unstable Cargo feature.

## If that gets annoying later

There's a third option I didn't offer as a question because it's a bigger structural change, but it's fully stable and needs *zero* IDE config: make `kernel/` its own workspace (`exclude = ["kernel"]` in the root `Cargo.toml` + a bare `[workspace]` in `kernel/Cargo.toml`). RustRover's `--workspace` then simply never sees the kernel. The costs are real though — a second `Cargo.lock` (so `audit`/`deny` no longer cover the kernel's deps from one lockfile), `cargo fmt --all` stops reaching it, and both `.cargo/config.toml` aliases need `--manifest-path kernel/Cargo.toml`. Worth revisiting only if the per-developer setup becomes a recurring friction point.

For the record, since it may matter for a future toolchain decision: `forced-target` did test clean on every gate including the QEMU boot, and it was the only option that made workspace clippy actually *lint* kernel code rather than skip it. The blocker was purely its unstable status, not its behavior.

content.text:
Branch is clean and back to PR #38 state. Two corrections to what I told you earlier, both now backed by tests:

**1. The IDE-only fix I suggested doesn't work.** `--exclude minixrs-kernel` is rejected because RustRover also generates `--features minixrs-kernel/boot-stubs,minixrs-kernel/default`, and cargo won't accept features for an excluded package. Making it work needs a *second* per-developer setting — unchecking the kernel's features in RustRover's Cargo tool window — which is fragile and easy to lose.

**2. I understated the nested-workspace cost.** I said "the costs are real though" and listed lockfile/fmt/aliases. Testing it, the first thing that breaks is the linker:

```
rust-lld: error: cannot find linker script kernel/src/arch/aarch64/linker.ld
```

With `kernel/` as its own workspace root, rustc's cwd changes, so the relative linker-script path in `.cargo/config.toml` breaks. Beyond that it also needs `[profile.release]` (`panic = "abort"`, `opt-level = 's'`) duplicated into `kernel/Cargo.toml`, a `kernel/target/` gitignore entry, a committed second `Cargo.lock`, and extra CI invocations for `fmt`/`audit`/`deny` to keep covering the kernel. That's a genuinely large change to the build wiring.

## Where that leaves it

| Option | Fixes IDE | Stable | Churn |
|---|---|---|---|
| `forced-target` | ✅ zero config, all developers | ❌ unstable cargo feature | **3 lines** in `kernel/Cargo.toml` |
| Nested workspace | ✅ zero config, all developers | ✅ | linker wiring, profiles, 2nd lockfile, 3 CI jobs, aliases, docs |
| RustRover settings | ⚠️ 2 settings, per developer, undoable by accident | ✅ | none |
| Revert chunk 7 | ✅ | ✅ | gives up the PR |

You rejected `forced-target` on the premise that the IDE route would work with one setting. That premise was wrong, so the trade looks different now: it's the *only* option that is both zero-config and low-churn, and I've verified it passes every gate including the QEMU boot — its sole defect is the unstable flag, which your dated nightly pin already contains, and which fails loudly (a manifest error) rather than silently if a future bump drops it.

        run: rustup show
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
      - name: Install pinned toolchain

      # files plus 8 nested server builds on a blocking gate. Exclude it for
      # cost, not correctness: clippy-kernel below lints it natively on arm64,
      # and a local `cargo clippy --workspace` does lint it.
      - run: cargo clippy --workspace --exclude minixrs-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings

    name: clippy (kernel aarch64)
    # Native arm64 so the kernel's .S files assemble without a cross toolchain
    # (same reason qemu-smoke uses this runner).
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm

    # cost), so this job is the only CI job that lints and compiles kernel
    # code. The dated nightly pin in rust-toolchain.toml means a new lint can
    # only appear on a deliberate bump, so this can't red-X an unrelated PR.

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3
      - name: Install pinned toolchain

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497796c12c097a38f9edb9d0641fb99eee32 # v2

      # harness to build.

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # edition 2024, so a tooling breakage must not red-X the PR.
    continue-on-error: true

      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6.0.3

      - name: Install pinned toolchain

      - name: Install QEMU + aarch64 UEFI firmware

          # drive; it is a Recommends skipped by --no-install-recommends.

          qemu-system-aarch64 --version

      - name: Build kernel

      - name: Boot in QEMU (45 s wall clock)

The exec target is a freestanding `userland/worker` ELF (getpid loop + `PM_EXIT`; **no** `server-rt`/SEF — a plain user program, deps `minix-ipc` + `kernel-shared` only), packed into the MXBI archive by `build.rs` with sentinel proc_nr `com::EXEC_ONLY_PROC_NR = -1` — the boot loader (`userland.rs` load loop) skips any negative proc_nr, so `worker` is resolvable by name but **never boot-loaded** (no `[as]` line, no proc/priv slot). PM's `execve` hardcodes `EXEC_TARGET = "worker"` for the demo (a user-supplied path arrives with Phase-5 musl/filesystem; the kernel path is already name-driven). Stub E's child branch flips `PM_EXIT` → `PM_EXEC`: fork → child execs `worker` → worker exits → parent reaps → loop, so a `[ksys SYS_EXEC] target=16 name=worker` per cycle sits between the `SYS_FORK`/`SYS_EXIT nr=16` twins with a monotonically advancing endpoint generation + recycled ASID (exec teardown + reap proof). `userland/**/src/main.rs` added to `sonar.coverage.exclusions` (freestanding entry point, QEMU-verified, no host-testable logic — like the server `main.rs`es)

- The demo stubs A–D are gated behind a **`boot-stubs` cargo feature (default-on)** — `--no-default-features` gives a clean, stub-free boot (servers + init/worker only) for debugging (chunk-3 prep). The feature lives on **two crates**, the kernel (gates `arch::aarch64::userland`'s stub code) and PM (gates `mproc::seed`'s stub loop), because those are the only two that install/seed stubs. `kernel/build.rs` reads `CARGO_FEATURE_BOOT_STUBS` to (a) drop `user_stub.S` from the assembly `sources` and (b) pass `--no-default-features` to the *nested* PM build (the nested build has its own feature resolution, so the flag must be threaded through), keeping kernel and PM in lockstep. The feature is deliberately **not** on `kernel-shared`: a shared-crate default feature gets force-enabled by other dependents (`minix-ipc`, `server-rt`) via cargo **feature unification**, making it impossible to turn off — so `NR_STUB_PROCS` stays a constant `4` and `FORK_POOL_BASE` (= 15) is stable; disabling stubs just leaves slots 11–14 unoccupied, it doesn't renumber the fork pool

- User-process capacity is one shared constant (chunk-4 prep): `kernel-shared::com::NR_SERVED_PROCS` (= 32) is the exclusive proc-nr ceiling the user-space servers track, and all three per-process server tables derive their size from it — PM `mproc` (`NR_MPROCS = NR_SERVED_PROCS`, proc-nr-indexed), VM `ClientRegions` (`MAX_CLIENTS = NR_SERVED_PROCS`, proc-nr-indexed), and SCHED `policy` (`CAP = NR_SERVED_PROCS`, an *associative* count, not proc-nr-indexed, so `NR_SERVED_PROCS` over-covers the delegatable set). Never reintroduce independent capacity literals: each crate carries a `const _: () = assert!(… >= NR_SERVED_PROCS)` guard (plus `NR_SERVED_PROCS <= NR_PROCS` and `> NR_BOOT_PROCS + NR_STUB_PROCS` in com.rs) so an under-sized local edit fails at compile time. VM `MAX_REGIONS` (regions per client, heap + mmaps) is a separate knob (= 16), unrelated to the kernel frame allocator's like-named `MAX_REGIONS` in `mm/frame.rs`

- Feature-toggle debugging: when a `--no-default-features` build doesn't actually drop a feature, suspect cargo **feature unification** — diagnose with `cargo tree -p <crate> --no-default-features -e features -i <shared-crate>` (inverted tree shows *who* still activates it) or `cargo tree -p <crate> -f "{p} {f}"` (feature set per crate)

The kernel builds against the **builtin `aarch64-unknown-none` target** — not a
custom JSON spec. `.cargo/config.toml` wires the details:

```toml
[target.aarch64-unknown-none]
runner   = "tools/qemu-run.sh"
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-Tkernel/src/arch/aarch64/linker.ld"]

[alias]
kernel-aarch64 = "build -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release"
```

The `x86_64-unknown-none` target and its `kernel-x86_64` alias are scaffolding for
the planned port; the kernel does not boot on x86_64 yet.

The crate stays a workspace `members` entry — one shared `Cargo.lock` keeps `audit` /
`deny` covering its dependencies, and `cargo fmt --all` still formats it (cargo-fmt
enumerates all members, and rustfmt follows `mod` declarations without evaluating
`cfg`) — but it is **omitted from `default-members`**:

```sh
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings          # skips the kernel
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets             # DOES build the kernel -> error
cargo clippy --workspace --exclude minixrs-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings   # ok
```

`--workspace` overrides `default-members`, so workspace-wide invocations must pass
`--exclude minixrs-kernel`; CI's `clippy` and `coverage` jobs do. A host build that
slips through fails with a single message from `build.rs` naming `cargo kernel-aarch64`
(a `#[cfg(not(target_os = "none"))] compile_error!` in `main.rs` states the same
invariant at the source). No `cfg(target_os = ...)` gates remain under `kernel/src/`.

> **rust-analyzer:** its default check is `cargo check --workspace`, which will report
> the kernel's guard as an error. Add
> `"rust-analyzer.check.extraArgs": ["--exclude", "minixrs-kernel"]` to your editor
> settings.
input.new_string:
Rather than hide the crate from workspace commands, `kernel/Cargo.toml` pins its
build target:

```toml
cargo-features = ["per-package-target"]

[package]
forced-target = "aarch64-unknown-none"

[[bin]]
name = "minixrs-kernel"
path = "src/main.rs"
test = false      # no_std/no_main: a --test build needs the `test` crate (std)
bench = false
```

Every cargo invocation therefore cross-compiles the kernel instead of failing on it —
bare or `--workspace`, and from any IDE:

```sh
cargo check --workspace --all-targets     # ok: kernel cross-compiled
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets    # ok, and it genuinely LINTS kernel code
cargo test --workspace                    # ok: kernel has no test target
```

That last point is the payoff: kernel code is now visible to the lint gates instead of
merely hidden from them. `forced-target` wins even over an explicit
`--target x86_64-apple-darwin`, so a host build is unreachable, and no `--exclude` or
per-developer editor setting is required.

Three things to know:

- **`per-package-target` is unstable** ([cargo#9406](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/9406)),
  hence the `cargo-features` opt-in and the nightly pin in `rust-toolchain.toml`. If a
  future bump drops it, cargo fails loudly on the manifest; the fallback is a workspace
  `default-members` list omitting `"kernel"`.
- **`test = false` is required.** Without it, `cargo check --all-targets` builds a
  phantom test harness for the kernel bin and fails with `E0463: can't find crate for test`.
- `build.rs`'s `cargo::error=` and `main.rs`'s `#[cfg(not(target_os = "none"))] compile_error!`
  are now unreachable defense-in-depth, kept in case `forced-target` ever stops applying.

No `cfg(target_os = ...)` gates remain under `kernel/src/`.

input.command:
git add -A && git status --short && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Pin the kernel's build target instead of hiding it from host builds

The `default-members` + `--exclude minixrs-kernel` approach kept CI green but
broke IDEs. RustRover's external linter runs

  cargo check --all-targets --workspace \
    --features minixrs-kernel/boot-stubs,minixrs-kernel/default

and there is no one-setting fix for it: adding `--exclude minixrs-kernel` makes
cargo reject the command outright ("none of the selected packages contains
these features"), because the feature flags name the excluded package. Fixing
it in the IDE needs two fragile per-developer settings.

Replace the exclusion with a per-package target pin:

  cargo-features = ["per-package-target"]
  [package] forced-target = "aarch64-unknown-none"
  [[bin]] test = false, bench = false

Every cargo invocation now cross-compiles the kernel rather than failing on it
-- bare, `--workspace`, or from any IDE -- with no per-developer config. This
wins even over an explicit `--target x86_64-apple-darwin`, so a host build is
unreachable rather than merely discouraged, and `default-members` is dropped:
with the target pinned there is no reason to hide the crate, and hiding it
would only make a bare `cargo clippy` skip kernel code again. A local
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` now genuinely *lints* the kernel
(verified with a deliberate canary), so chunk 7's blind spot is closed rather
than relocated.

`test = false` on the bin is required: without it `--all-targets` builds a
phantom test harness for a no_std/no_main crate and fails with E0463.

Costs, accepted deliberately:

- `per-package-target` is unstable (rust-lang/cargo#9406). It needs the nightly
  already pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, and a bump that drops it fails loudly
  on the manifest -- the fallback is the `default-members` list this replaces.
- It overrides `--target` in an alias, so `cargo kernel-x86_64` would have
  silently built aarch64. That alias is removed; Phase 8 must relax
  `forced-target` before restoring it.

A nested workspace (`exclude = ["kernel"]`) was prototyped as the stable
alternative and rejected: it breaks the relative linker-script path in
.cargo/config.toml (`rust-lld: cannot find linker script`), and additionally
needs the release profile duplicated, a second committed Cargo.lock, a
kernel/target gitignore entry, and separate fmt/audit/deny CI invocations.

CI keeps `--exclude minixrs-kernel` on `clippy` and `coverage`, now for runner
cost rather than correctness: building the kernel there would mean clang
cross-assembling the .S files plus 8 nested server builds on a blocking x86
gate. `clippy-kernel` on the native arm runner remains the kernel gate and now
also proves `per-package-target` still resolves.

Verified: the exact RustRover command passes; fmt, workspace clippy (with and
without the exclusion), kernel clippy in both feature configs, and
`cargo test -p minixrs-kernel-shared` (54 passed) all green; both QEMU boots
pass (default 24/24 markers, stub-free 7 servers + init, no panics).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
